title: Asana API Guide: Get Tasks, Projects, and Users in 2026
summary: Asana API retrieves tasks using personal access tokens via REST calls.
body_markdown:
## Asana API rate limits and pricing, as documented


You pay for every page in requests. Asana caps them at 1,500 per minute on a paid domain, 150 on a free domain and 60 for the Search API, according to[Asana's rate-limits page](https://developers.asana.com/docs/rate-limits) .


> **A loop that reads only the first page will pass every test on a small project and silently drop tasks on a large one.


### What Asana API rate limits mean in practice


At 150 requests per minute on a free domain, a project with 10,000 tasks, paged at 100 per request, uses about 100 calls for one full read.


A second read in the same minute would exceed your quota, so you may need to wait for the Retry-After period before refreshing that data.


Move to a paid domain at 1,500 and you get roughly ten times that room.


Tightest of all is the Search API at 60 per minute. A workflow that searches once per task will stall after one minute's worth of tasks and need backoff on the 429 responses.


These are the only limits I have confirmed figures for. Asana's page also covers concurrent-request and cost-based limits, which this article doesn't quote, so read that page before sizing a bulk job. Figures checked 2026-11-20.


### What API access costs


You won't find a per-call price in the documentation. Access appears to come with the plan, so the cost is the seat price.[G2's Asana pricing page](https://www.g2.com/products/asana/pricing) lists **Personal at $0 per user per month** , Starter at $10.99 and Advanced at $24.99.


Because Personal is free, you can build and test against the API at no cost, but it sits under the 150-per-minute free ceiling. Starter at $10.99 per user is the cheapest tier listed above that free plan.


### Which Asana plan to build on


Since the 1,500 figure applies to paid domains, a production sync is better planned on a paid plan. Asana's rate-limits page doesn't tie the cap to a specific tier, so confirm which plan your workspace is on before you rely on it.


Treat the pricing figures as a snapshot, since they come from a third-party listing rather than Asana's own pricing page.
